plan: Ten new items; every topic and choice set checked against the live bank (perfunctory, derivative and an 'Accordingly' transition were avoided because 149/160, 125/223 and 327 use them). superficial/intransigent WIC, dandelion vortex purpose, Koshima macaque inference, lake ice-cover rate data (unequal time spans), pea-root sound hypothesis evidence, Yellowstone wolves cross-text, Wangari Maathai synthesis, 'In response' transition, comma after long introductory phrase.

passages.title: A quick inspection
passages.text: The auditor's review of the contracts was ______: she glanced at the first page of each one and signed off without checking any of the figures inside.

passages.title: Stalled talks
passages.text: After six weeks of negotiations, both sides remained ______: the union refused to lower its wage demand by even a single percentage point, and the company would not raise its offer at all.

passages.title: Floating seeds
passages.text: A dandelion seed travels on a pappus, a tuft of about a hundred fine bristles. Engineers long assumed that such a sparse structure could not create much drag. In 2018, however, researchers using wind tunnels found that air flowing through the gaps between the bristles forms a stable ring of swirling air just above the seed, a kind of vortex never before seen in nature. This ring slows the seed's fall, letting it drift for long distances while using very little material.

passages.title: Washing potatoes
passages.text: In 1953, researchers on the Japanese island of Koshima saw a young female macaque named Imo wash a sandy sweet potato in a stream before eating it. Over the next few years, the behavior spread first to Imo's playmates and her mother, then to the playmates' mothers, and eventually to most of the troop. The adult males, who spent the least time near the young monkeys, were the slowest to adopt it, and some never did. This pattern suggests that ______

passages.title: Shrinking ice
passages.text:
A lake's average number of ice-covered days per winter was recorded over more than a century.
Period | Average ice-covered days
1900s | 120
1950s | 110
2000s | 95
2010s | 88
A researcher claimed that ice cover has not only declined but has declined faster in recent decades than in the early twentieth century.

passages.title: Roots and running water
passages.text: Plant roots grow toward moisture in the soil. Biologist Monica Gagliano wondered whether roots might also respond to the sound of water. She hypothesized that pea roots can grow toward the sound of flowing water even when no moisture difference guides them.

passages.title: Wolves and willows (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
After gray wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone National Park in 1995, willows along many streams began to recover. Some ecologists attributed this to a "landscape of fear": elk, wary of wolves, avoided lingering along open streambanks, so they browsed less on young willows.
Text 2
Later studies found that elk numbers in the park had also fallen because of hunting outside the park, growing populations of bears and cougars, and drought. In several areas, elk did not noticeably avoid risky streambanks, and willows recovered only where elk numbers had dropped sharply.

passages.title: Wangari Maathai
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Wangari Maathai was a Kenyan biologist and environmental activist.
• In 1977, she founded the Green Belt Movement.
• The movement paid women in rural communities to plant trees.
• Its members have planted tens of millions of trees across Kenya.
• In 2004, Maathai became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

passages.title: A rover powers down
passages.text: The rover's battery output had fallen below the level engineers considered safe for driving. ______ mission controllers put it into a low-power sleep mode until the Martian spring brought stronger sunlight to its solar panels.

passages.title: Roads in the mountains
passages.text: Stretching for tens of thousands of kilometers across the Andes______ the Inca road system linked an empire that had no wheeled vehicles and no horses.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: signed off without checking any of the figures inside
candidates.explanation: A review that looks only at the surface and checks nothing in depth is "superficial."

B.rationale: Glancing at one page and checking no figures is the opposite of exhaustive.

C.rationale: Nothing suggests the auditor was unfriendly or opposed.

D.rationale: Nothing about the review is new or creative.

candidates.remember: The detail after the colon defines the blank.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: would not raise its offer at all
candidates.explanation: Two parties that refuse to change their positions at all are "intransigent."

A.rationale: Refusing to budge at all is the opposite of conciliatory.

B.rationale: Both sides held firm positions; they were not uninterested.

D.rationale: Neither side showed mixed feelings; each was firmly fixed.

hints: Would either side give any ground?
candidates.remember: Use both examples after the colon to define the blank.

candidates.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that engineers should copy the structure of dandelion seeds when designing wind tunnels
choices.B: To describe how a surprising airflow pattern explains the dandelion seed's ability to stay aloft
choices.C: To compare the seeds of dandelions with the seeds of several other wind-dispersed plants
choices.D: To explain why each dandelion seed has about a hundred bristles rather than a larger number

candidates.evidence: This ring slows the seed's fall
candidates.explanation: The text sets up an assumption about sparse bristles, then reports the vortex discovery that explains how the seed stays aloft.

A.rationale: The text never makes a recommendation about wind tunnels.

D.rationale: The number of bristles is mentioned only as a description, not explained.

strategy.explanation: Summarize the problem and the finding.

candidates.remember: Purpose questions ask what the whole text accomplishes.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: adult male macaques are completely unable to learn any new behaviors once they reach maturity.
choices.B: the macaques washed their potatoes mainly because the researchers rewarded them with extra food.
choices.C: Imo herself learned to wash potatoes by carefully watching older members of the troop.
choices.D: the behavior spread mainly through close social contact rather than being invented separately by each monkey.

candidates.evidence: who spent the least time near the young monkeys, were the slowest to adopt it
candidates.explanation: The behavior moved along lines of close contact (playmates, mothers) and reached the least-connected males last, which points to social learning.

A.rationale: Some adult males did adopt the behavior, just slowly; the text links the delay to less contact.

B.rationale: The text says nothing about rewards for washing.

C.rationale: Imo was the first to do it; the others learned after her.

hints: Who adopted it first, and who last?

strategy.explanation: Trace the order of spread before reading the choices.

candidates.remember: When a pattern follows social ties, the cause is likely social.

author_checklist.hardness: Requires linking the order of spread to contact patterns and rejecting the overstated male-learning claim.

candidates.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researcher's claim?

choices.A: Ice cover fell from an average of 120 days in the 1900s to 88 days in the 2010s, an overall decline of 32 days.
choices.B: Ice cover in the 2010s, at an average of 88 days per winter, was lower than in any other period shown in the table.
choices.C: Ice cover fell 10 days over the five decades from the 1900s to the 1950s but 7 days in the one decade from the 2000s to the 2010s.
choices.D: Ice cover fell by only 7 days from the 2000s to the 2010s, less than the 15-day drop from the 1950s to the 2000s.

candidates.evidence: has declined faster in recent decades than in the early twentieth century
candidates.explanation: The claim concerns the rate of decline. A drop of 10 days over fifty years (about 2 per decade) versus 7 days in one decade shows the rate rising sharply in recent decades.

A.rationale: This shows an overall decline but not that the rate of decline increased.

B.rationale: This shows the latest value is lowest but says nothing about the rate of change.

D.rationale: This compares raw totals over a ten-year and a fifty-year span; per decade, the recent drop is actually much larger, so this misreads the data and suggests the opposite of the claim.

hints: Is the claim about the amount of decline or its speed?

strategy.explanation: Compare changes per decade, not totals.

candidates.remember: A claim about rate needs changes divided by time.

author_checklist.hardness: Requires comparing rates over unequal time spans.

candidates.subskill: Command of evidence: textual (supporting a hypothesis)
candidates.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Gagliano's hypothesis?

choices.A: In sealed pots with evenly moist soil, roots grew toward a recording of flowing water played beside one side of the pot.
choices.B: Roots grew toward the wetter side of a pot in which one side had been watered more heavily than the other.
choices.C: Pea plants grown near noisy machinery produced fewer seeds than plants grown in quiet rooms.
choices.D: Roots grew straight downward when pots were placed in a completely silent and evenly moist room.

candidates.evidence: even when no moisture difference guides them
candidates.explanation: The hypothesis requires a response to sound with moisture held equal; A removes the moisture difference and still shows roots growing toward the sound.

B.rationale: This shows a response to moisture, which the hypothesis specifically sets aside.

C.rationale: This concerns noise and seed production, not roots growing toward water sounds.

D.rationale: This shows what roots do without sound but not that they move toward a water sound.

hints: What must the finding rule out?

strategy.explanation: Identify the factor the hypothesis isolates.

candidates.remember: The best support isolates the exact factor in the hypothesis.

author_checklist.hardness: Requires rejecting the moisture-gradient result the hypothesis excludes.

candidates.stem: Based on the texts, how would the authors of the later studies in Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that elk avoided open streambanks out of fear of wolves, since willows recovered in the park after 1995
choices.B: By arguing that a drop in elk numbers from several causes may explain willow recovery better than elk avoiding risky areas
choices.C: By arguing that the reintroduced wolves had no effect at all on the number of elk in the park
choices.D: By suggesting that willows along the park's streambanks did not actually recover at all after 1995

candidates.evidence: willows recovered only where elk numbers had dropped sharply
candidates.explanation: Text 2 points to fewer elk overall, from multiple causes, rather than fearful behavior, as what tracks willow recovery.

A.rationale: Text 2 reports that in several areas elk did not noticeably avoid streambanks.

C.rationale: Text 2 lists other causes but does not claim wolves had no effect.

D.rationale: Text 2 accepts that willows recovered in some areas.

hints: What does Text 2 say willow recovery tracked?
candidates.remember: An alternative explanation can accept the outcome but challenge its cause.

author_checklist.hardness: Requires separating 'fewer elk' from 'fearful elk' as competing causes.

candidates.stem: The student wants to emphasize the scale of the Green Belt Movement's work. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Wangari Maathai, a Kenyan biologist and activist, founded the Green Belt Movement in 1977.
choices.B: The Green Belt Movement, founded by Wangari Maathai, paid women in rural communities to plant trees.
choices.C: In 2004, Green Belt Movement founder Wangari Maathai became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.
choices.D: Since its founding in 1977, the Green Belt Movement has planted tens of millions of trees across Kenya.

candidates.evidence: Its members have planted tens of millions of trees across Kenya.
candidates.explanation: The goal is scale; only D gives the number of trees planted.

A.rationale: This gives the founder and date but not the scale of the work.

B.rationale: This explains how the movement worked but not how much it accomplished.

C.rationale: This emphasizes Maathai's honor, not the scale of the movement's work.

hints: Which note gives a sense of size?

strategy.explanation: Match the goal to the note with a quantity.

candidates.remember: Synthesis goals point to specific notes; find them first.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: had fallen below the level engineers considered safe
candidates.explanation: The first sentence states a problem; the second describes the controllers' reaction. "In response" signals that relationship.

A.rationale: Putting the rover to sleep is not done in spite of the low battery; it is done because of it.

B.rationale: No other option is described for this one to be an alternative to.

D.rationale: Powering down is not similar to the battery falling; it is a reaction to it.

hints: Is the second action caused by the first?
candidates.remember: Problem followed by action calls for a cause-and-response transition.

candidates.subskill: Comma after a long introductory phrase
candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: the Inca road system linked an empire
candidates.explanation: A long introductory participial phrase ("Stretching ... Andes") is followed by a comma before the subject it describes, "the Inca road system."

A.rationale: A semicolon must join two independent clauses; the opening phrase is not one.

C.rationale: A colon must follow an independent clause; the opening phrase is not one.

D.rationale: A dash does not set off an introductory phrase from the main clause; a comma is standard.

hints: Is the opening part a complete sentence?

strategy.explanation: Find where the main clause begins.

candidates.remember: Set off a long introductory phrase with a comma.
